advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an if-present guard (`[ -f tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py ] || { echo 'change predates the gate — skipping'; exit 0; }`) or a `# predates-gate-ok:` reason to the sandbox-enforcement pytest step so a pre-gate patchset skips instead of erroring.
evidence: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:372`: `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py \`
The Gerrit-lane checkout is present: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:326`: `uses: lfreleng-actions/checkout-gerrit-change-action@...`

`tests/unit/test_gate_step_tree_skew.py:5-11` states the invariant: 'A gate step that runs a repo script therefore runs against changes whose base predates that script, and dies with `can't open file ... [Errno 2]`'; PATCHSET_LANE_WORKFLOWS includes `_build-and-test.yml` (line 51) and `_SCRIPT_RE = re.compile(r"scripts/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.py")` (line 59) matches the `scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py` substring of the pytest path.
No `[ -f tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py ]` guard nor `# predates-gate-ok:` marker appears in the new step body (diff lines 361-374).
advisory.finding: The new `sandbox-enforcement` job runs `python -m pytest tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py` in the Gerrit patchset lane (checkout-gerrit-change-action) with no if-present (`-f`) guard on that path and no `# predates-gate-ok:` marker. On a patchset whose base predates the test file, the workflow definition comes from the target branch while the tree is the older patchset, so the file is absent and the step dies with Errno 2 — a hard CI failure indistinguishable from a real gate violation, exactly the definition-vs-tree skew the ee2a house rule forbids.
scenarios: Gerrit Verified lane on any change whose base commit predates tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py
advisory.suggested_fix: Wrap the pytest invocation: `if [ ! -f tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py ]; then echo 'test_mutation_sandbox.py not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping'; exit 0; fi` before running pytest inside the container, mirroring the dependency-audit step's guard.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Run the bwrap precondition probe in the same image the enforcement tests use (python:3.13-slim), or document why ubuntu:24.04 is a valid proxy.
evidence: Precondition runs in `ubuntu:24.04`: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:339`: `docker run --rm --privileged ubuntu:24.04 bash -c '`
Tests run in `python:3.13-slim`: `.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:366`: `python:3.13-slim bash -c '`

The test step is self-guarding — `_assert_child_ran` requires the child's liveness marker (tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:129) and `test_a_mechanism_is_required_when_the_lane_says_so` asserts `sb.probe() is not None` (line 83) — so a broken bwrap in slim fails loudly rather than false-passing.
advisory.finding: The precondition step proves bwrap can namespace/enforce inside `ubuntu:24.04`, but the enforcement tests actually run inside a different image (`python:3.13-slim`). A passing precondition in ubuntu:24.04 does not establish that bwrap namespacing works in python:3.13-slim, so the load-bearing precondition guards a different environment than the one under test.
scenarios: bwrap behaves differently between ubuntu:24.04 and python:3.13-slim (e.g. missing suid/apparmor profile)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test proving that with REBAR_REQUIRE_SANDBOX_ENFORCEMENT=1 and probe() forced to None, a @live enforcement test executes (and fails) rather than skips, so the added skipif clause is regression-guarded.
evidence: tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:69-72: `live = pytest.mark.skipif(\n    sb.probe() is None and not REQUIRE_ENFORCEMENT,`
tests/scripts/test_mutation_sandbox.py:83: the new test asserts only `assert sb.probe() is not None`, which observes mechanism presence, not the skipif clause's effect on the @live tests

Named violating input: REBAR_REQUIRE_SANDBOX_ENFORCEMENT=1 with sb.probe() returning None — the added clause should make a @live test run and fail, but no test drives this combination; the constant is import-time-bound so it is not exercised by any monkeypatch
Ticket 0d22-f664 AC: 'The requirement flag is proven load-bearing: with it set and probe() forced to return None, the enforcement tests FAIL. Demonstrated by real substitution.'
advisory.finding: The added `and not REBAR_REQUIRE_SANDBOX_ENFORCEMENT` clause on the `live` skipif marker (the change's load-bearing behavior: flag set + probe() None => `@live` enforcement tests run instead of skip) has no regression test. The new test only asserts `sb.probe() is not None`; it never verifies that with the flag set and no mechanism a `@live` test actually executes-and-fails rather than skips. This is exactly the AC 'requirement flag is proven load-bearing... with it set and probe() forced to return None, the enforcement tests FAIL... by real substitution', which is left unverified. Because the skipif condition is evaluated once at import against a module-level constant, a later refactor that broke the not-skip path would pass every test on the (bwrap-working) CI lane where probe() is non-None.

Comment claims "MEASURED (ubuntu:24.04, bubblewrap 0.9.0)" (line 307) but nothing pins bwrap to 0.9.0 or images to a digest.
advisory.finding: The enforcement lane runs `docker run --privileged` twice; `--privileged` grants the container full host capabilities/device access, a maximal blast radius that is broader than the namespace/user-ns capability the test actually needs.
merged_from: Base images and the apt bubblewrap package are unpinned mutable references (`ubuntu:24.04`, `python:3.13-slim`, `apt-get install bubblewrap`), so the lane is not reproducible and can drift away from the 'measured on bubblewrap 0.9.0' guarantee the comment relies on.
scenarios: A compromised or malicious base image / installed apt package escapes to the GitHub-hosted runner host via privileged mode.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the privileged sandbox-enforcement lane never runs untrusted (fork PR / unmerged patchset) code, or drop `--privileged` for the workspace-mounted run.
evidence: `pip install -q ".[dev]"`
Workflow header: "test.yml's pull_request trigger includes fork PRs" (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:18-19)
Contrast: lint job runs `uv lock --check` and `uv sync --locked --extra dev` (.github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml:69,72)
advisory.finding: The second privileged container bind-mounts the checked-out change (`-v "$PWD:/w"`) and executes code from it (`pip install ".[dev]"`, pytest), so untrusted change-under-review code runs inside a `--privileged` container — on the branch/PR lane this includes fork pull_request checkouts.
merged_from: `pip install ".[dev]"` inside the container resolves dependencies unpinned, bypassing the committed `uv.lock` the rest of the workflow enforces (`uv lock --check` / `uv sync --locked`), reintroducing dependency drift on this lane.
scenarios: A fork PR or Gerrit patchset adds a malicious setup hook / dev dependency that executes with full host capabilities during install/test.
